subject: Load failures in build-output.test.ts, self-corpus.test.ts and durable-lifecycle.test.ts (apps/three-surface-poc); draft-preview.browser excluded (syzygy-za9v)

measuredAt.note: Measured at c27fbf4 (rebased on ab22492). Mutants ran at an unpushed working commit with identical test-file blobs; any later rebase re-hashes the commit, so the blobs are the stable anchor.

classes.over: 46 loaded reports (syzygy-4d15 before/after and syzygy-pln3 after, measured and companion)

build-output.test.ts.timeoutCause: Two sequential forced tsc -b builds of five projects: about 14-15 s alone, median 56 s and worst 69.9 s under the parallel-load protocol, against the 60 s limit set by syzygy-gk9.
build-output.test.ts.interferenceCause: The test poisoned the checkout's shared apps/three-surface-poc/dist/main.js between two builds. A second test run in the same checkout (the protocol's companion, or a second session) could read the other's poison after its own rebuild (poisoned read) or collide with its build (failed build). Not a timeout.

interferenceReproduction.note: Two concurrent runs of the build test, three trials each, with a cross-process lock (an intermediate design, since replaced) and without it.

results.message: AssertionError: expected 'throw new Error("poisoned ignored POC…' not to contain 'throw new Error("poisoned ignored POC…

build-output.test.ts.crashHazard: [Observed] Killing a run of the intermediate lock version mid-test left dist/main.js containing the poison line and a stale lock. A lock serializes concurrent runs but cannot repair a crash between poison and rebuild; a later 'npm run poc' rebuilds first, but a direct 'node apps/three-surface-poc/dist/main.js' would run the poison. The checkout was rebuilt and the lock removed.
build-output.test.ts.fix: The test now copies the working-tree root files and apps/ and packages/ (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, so uncommitted edits are included) into a private temporary directory, runs npm ci there (2 s and 55 MB from a warm cache at load 33), and builds, poisons and rebuilds only that copy; the copy is removed in finally. The checkout's dist/main.js was byte- and mtime-identical across a run. Per-test timeout 240 s (two builds' measured worst 69.9 s plus copy and install; a cold npm cache costs more). No assertion changed.

self-corpus.test.ts.cause: 'reads only tracked blobs from the pinned commit' runs the production readSelfCorpus, which spawns one git cat-file per selected blob (over a hundred at the pinned commit; same pattern as syzygy-pln3 and the svoj follow-up). About 0.9-1.0 s alone in the after runs; median 4.6 s and worst 7.8 s under load, against the default 5 s.
self-corpus.test.ts.fix: Explicit per-test timeout PINNED_READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 with a comment; the read is the subject of the test, so it cannot be hoisted or replaced.

durable-lifecycle.test.ts.cause: Fixed small workload (scripted pipeline over a journal that fsyncs every write: 10, 10, 2 and 20 fsync calls per test by strace; about 0.3 s alone). Under one concurrent full run at load 19-23, six strace runs measured 42 fsyncs totalling 0.50-0.89 s with the worst single fsync 50 ms, and test durations under 0.6 s. The 6.3 s outlier (2 of 46 executions of one test) is therefore [Inferred] a host stall rather than a cost in the test.
durable-lifecycle.test.ts.fix: Explicit per-test timeout JOURNAL_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000 on all four tests, with a comment.

protocol: As syzygy-4d15: each measured full app-project run ran concurrently with one companion full run in the same worktree, alongside the other lane's load; load1m sampled at each run's end. Timeout classifier: failure message starting 'Error: STACK_TRACE_ERROR' or containing 'timed out in'.

before.note: Test files and the two loaders had the same blobs at 0170bfc, fd8d1a2, bb6b893 and this branch's base.

after.statement: 10 consecutive full app-project runs, each with a concurrent companion (20 reports): 180 in-scope executions (9 tests x 20), 0 timeouts, 0 failures; every run and every companion exited with 0 failures across all 590 tests. Load at run end was 25.5-30.9, lower than the before runs' 30-43.
